fatal_errors: The proposed FeCoNiMnCu coating on SS-304 is not the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA, and the matched DS2205 comparator is omitted.
The proposed ambient 3.5 wt.% NaCl test does not reconstruct the temperature-dependent deionized-water experiment or its thermal-shock, load, and frequency comparisons.
A chromium-rich oxide is assigned to a nominally chromium-free Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 coating; the cited chromium oxide could instead arise from the SS-304 substrate or interdiffusion.
Thermally forming an oxide in one group and mechanically stripping it in another changes more than film integrity and does not isolate dynamic depassivation-repassivation during sliding.
explanation: The hypothesis captures one genuine element of the target mechanism: sliding-induced passive-film rupture, corrosion of exposed material, and film reformation can couple wear and corrosion. However, it omits the central nonmonotonic temperature competition among repassivation, polishing-layer stability, and oxide/third-body fracture, as well as the role of the thermally stable L12/B2 lamellar microstructure. It predicts only generic worsening after film damage, not the observed 50 °C minimum, the 50 °C < 25 °C < 100 °C ordering, or the substantially lower friction and wear of the HEA relative to identically treated DS2205. The baseline is not a matched material comparator and may collapse immediately once sliding removes the initially intact film. The cited studies support oxide-mediated corrosion or separate wear/corrosion improvements, but do not directly establish the proposed coupled tribocorrosion mechanism. A useful falsification experiment would instead control alloy state and prefilm chemistry while measuring transient OCP/current, repassivation, friction, and wear during identical sliding.
